best_facts.fact: In 1977 a drought on Daphne Major killed most medium ground finches. Survivors had beaks only about half a millimetre deeper, and their chicks inherited them.
best_facts.why_surprising: Evolution measurable with a ruler in a single year.

best_facts.fact: The closest known relative of whales, Indohyus, was a fox-sized hoofed animal from Kalakot in Jammu and Kashmir, and early whales also turn up in Kutch, Gujarat.
best_facts.why_surprising: Whales began as small land animals wading on India's ancient shoreline.

best_facts.fact: Human chromosome 2 is two ape chromosomes fused end to end, with leftover telomeres and a dead centromere in the middle.
best_facts.why_surprising: The fusion was predicted from common ancestry before it was found.

best_facts.fact: In Mozambique's Gorongosa park, tuskless females rose from about 18.5% before the civil war to about 51% of those born after, because poachers spared them.
best_facts.why_surprising: Hunting changed elephant anatomy in one generation.

best_facts.fact: Lenski's E. coli have been transferred to fresh broth every day since 24 February 1988 and passed 80,000 generations in 2024.
best_facts.why_surprising: About 2 million years of human generations, in a lab.

best_facts.fact: Cauliflower, cabbage, broccoli, kale, kohlrabi and Brussels sprouts are all one species, Brassica oleracea.
Tibetans' ability to live at high altitude without thick blood comes largely from a gene inherited from Denisovans.
best_facts.why_surprising: An extinct human cousin helps people breathe on the plateau.

best_facts.fact: Five pairs of lizards moved to a Croatian islet in 1971 evolved a new gut structure, cecal valves, within about 36 years.
best_facts.why_surprising: A new anatomical feature, in decades not millennia.

best_facts.fact: The word 'evolution' does not appear in the first edition of On the Origin of Species. The last word of the book is 'evolved'.
best_facts.why_surprising: The most famous book on evolution avoided the word.

best_facts.fact: Selecting silver foxes only for tameness also gave them floppy ears, curly tails and piebald coats.
On Pingelap atoll, about 1 in 10 people are totally colour-blind, against roughly 1 in 30,000 elsewhere, because of a typhoon around 1775.
best_facts.why_surprising: A storm 250 years ago still shapes how a whole island sees.

best_facts.fact: Unrelated cheetahs can accept each other's skin grafts, like identical twins.
best_facts.why_surprising: The whole species is nearly genetically uniform.

best_facts.fact: Darwin's 'I think' notebook went missing for about 20 years and was returned anonymously in a pink gift bag in 2022.
best_facts.why_surprising: The birthplace of the tree of life came back with an Easter note.

best_facts.fact: J. B. S. Haldane, a founder of evolutionary genetics, moved to Kolkata in 1957 and became an Indian citizen in 1961.
best_facts.why_surprising: Evolutionary theory has an Indian chapter few people know.

best_facts.fact: Bajau sea nomads have spleens about 50% larger than their land-farming neighbours, an adaptation to free diving.
best_facts.why_surprising: Natural selection shaping humans within recorded history.

best_facts.fact: Nilsson and Pelger's pessimistic model said a camera eye could evolve from a flat light patch in about 364,000 generations.
best_facts.why_surprising: The 'too complex to evolve' organ is quick in geological time.

best_facts.fact: On the mega-plate, E. coli evolved resistance to about 1,000 times the lethal antibiotic dose in about 11 days.
best_facts.why_surprising: Resistance can build in days, not years.

best_facts.fact: Colossal's 2025 'dire wolves' carry no ancient dire wolf DNA; they are grey wolves with about 20 edits in 14 genes.
best_facts.why_surprising: The headline and the biology did not match.

side_dish.title: Your doctor is fighting evolution
side_dish.body_md:
Every time you take an antibiotic, you run a natural selection experiment inside your own body. Billions of bacteria meet the drug. Most die. Any that happen to carry a resistance mutation, or picked up a resistance gene from a neighbour on a plasmid, survive and multiply with the competition gone.

That is why doctors tell you to finish a course, and why using antibiotics for viral colds is harmful: it selects for resistance without curing anything. Farms that dose healthy animals with antibiotics to speed growth run the same experiment at scale.

India sits at the centre of this. It is one of the world's largest consumers of antibiotics, and many have been sold without prescription. In 2016 the government's **Red Line** campaign began marking prescription-only antibiotic packs with a red vertical line, telling buyers not to take them without a doctor's advice. Kerala launched a state action plan on antimicrobial resistance in 2018.

The same logic shapes cancer treatment. A tumour is a population of cells that vary; chemotherapy kills the sensitive ones and can leave resistant cells to regrow. Some oncologists now try 'adaptive therapy', dosing just enough to keep sensitive cells around to compete with resistant ones, using evolution against itself.

Once you see medicine as applied evolution, a lot of advice makes sense: vaccines that need updating, drug cocktails for HIV and TB that make resistance to all at once unlikely, and why new antibiotics are precious and hoarded.

offline_task.title: Find evolution in your kitchen and street
offline_task.body_md:
Spend 20 minutes looking for evolution in ordinary life.

1. **The sabzi test.** At the market or in your fridge, find as many Brassica oleracea forms as you can: cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, kohlrabi. Hold two side by side. Same species. Ask which part of the plant each one exaggerates.
2. **The dog test.** Watch street dogs and pet breeds. Indian street dogs, the 'pariah' type, look much like each other and like early dogs; pet breeds vary wildly. Which looks more like the work of natural selection, and which like human choice?
3. **The pigeon test.** Look at a flock of feral pigeons. Count the colour forms: blue-grey with two black bars, chequered, dark, reddish. All are descendants of the rock dove, many from escaped domestic birds.
4. **The medicine cabinet.** Check any antibiotic strip at home for a red vertical line. That line exists because of evolution.

Write one sentence for each in a notebook. You will remember the forces through the things you touched.
